header.running_head: The Lectures Rasulullaah ﷺ Delivered on the Occasion of Hajj

blocks.text:
"This is a sacred city," the Sahabah (RA) responded. When Rasulullaah ﷺ further asked them what month it was, they replied that the month was also a sacred one. Rasulullaah ﷺ then emphasised, "Verily, your blood, your wealth and your honour are as sacred to you as this day, this city and this month." After repeating this several times, Rasulullaah ﷺ looked to the sky and said, "O Allaah! Have I conveyed the message? O Allaah! Have I conveyed the message?"
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life that an emphatic piece of advice that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave to the Ummah was that he said, 'Those of you present here should convey the message to those who are not present and you should never become Kuffaar after my death by striking the necks of each other (by killing each other).'"[^1]

Hadhrat Jareer (RA) narrates that after asking him to keep the people quiet (on the occasion of the Farewell Hajj), Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed them saying, "After I have been keeping watch over you, never become Kuffaar after my death by striking the necks of each other (by killing each other)."[^2]

Hadhrat Ummul Husayn (RA) reports that when she performed the Farewell Hajj with Rasulullaah ﷺ she saw Hadhrat Usaamah (RA) and Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) with Rasulullaah ﷺ. One of them was holding the reins of his camel while the other was holding his shawl aloft to shade Rasulullaah ﷺ from the sun until he had pelted the last Jamarah. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said many things, amongst which Hadhrat Ummul Husayn (RA) heard him say, "Even if an Abyssinian slave with amputated limbs has to become your ruler, you should listen to and obey him if he leads you by the Book of Allaah."[^3]

Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that on the occasion of the Farewell Hajj, he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say the following in his sermon: "Allaah has granted every rightful person his right. Therefore, no bequest can be made for an heir, a child will belong to the biological father and the adulterer will be stoned. Their reckoning will nevertheless be Allaah's prerogative. The curse of Allaah perpetuating until the Day of Qiyaamah shall fall on the person who claims to be the child of anyone other than his father and on the slave who claims to be the property of anyone other than his master. A woman my also not spend from the house without the permission of her husband." Someone asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Can she not even give food away (without his permission)?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "(Certainly not because) Food is the best of our wealth." Rasulullaah ﷺ then continued to say, "Items given on loan must be returned, animals lent to give milk must also be returned, debts must be paid and the guarantor must settle the penalty."[^4] Another narration makes it clear that the lecture was delivered in Mina on the day of Nahr (10th of Dhul Hijjah).[^5]

Bukhaari, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.5 Pg.194). Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Maajah, Tabraani and Baghawi have all reported similar narrations from various Sahabah (RA), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.25).
Ahmad, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.5 Pg.197).
Muslim, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.5 Pg.196). Nasa'ee has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.62), as has Ibn Sa'd (Vol.2 Pg.184).
Ahmad, Tirmidhi, Abu Dawood, Nasa'ee and Ibn Maajah.
